title: Control of blackjack in annual crop fields - Vietnam

Header: Control of blackjack in annual crop fields - Vietnam
Bidens pilosa Đơn buốt, Dần sàng, Quỷchâm, Cúc áo

Prevention: Purchase and sow certified crop seeds to reduce the chance of contamination.
Seeds are spread by animals - do not allow livestock into an affected area to avoid spread.
Seeds are spread on clothes and shoes - remove seeds when leaving an infested area.
Seeds are spread by water - use only water from sources free of the weed; use filter net to eliminate seeds from irrigation water; avoid runoff from surrounding infested fields.
Seeds spread by wind - limit seed set in surrounding populations.
Use crop rotation with paddy rice annually, if applicable.
A maize-bean, sweet potato intercropping system can effectively suppress the weed.
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: annual crops such as maize, vegetables, soybean, groundnut, cassava
Annual erect broadleaved weed (up to 1m high) with green composed leaves and a strong taproot.
Flowers white with yellow centre and 1-1.5 cm long black slender seeds, ribbed, dry, one seeded, with 2-4 yellowish barbed bristles or awns at one end.
Inspect surrounding fields weekly for the presence of the weed.
Check fields weekly for infestation and consider direct control if the weed is present.
Check weekly for the flowering of the weed and seed development to prevent seed set, spread and build-up of seed bank.
Direct Control: Dig up 5-10cm or hand-pull plants prior to the onset of flowering, ensuring the taproot is severed well below the crown to prevent regrowth.
Mow or slash the species prior to flowering and seed set to prevent further spread.
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
3000g a.i/ha), once before or immediately after sowing/planting of the crop.
Apply translocated herbicides metsulfuron methyl (12-15g a.i/ha), glyphosate (960-1200g a.i./ha) or 2,4-D (720-900g a.i/ ha) once/crop season after harvesting, if the weed is present on the field.
Do not use the herbicide on fields with growing crops.
U (unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use), WSSA resistance group 2.
